sourceContext: Human explicitly authorizes ORCHESTOR core to continue autonomously from the existing bootstrap/runtime state until it becomes a clean reusable installable multi-project agent. This supersedes the earlier core-completion command by adding the final product/UX/multi-task completion target and explicitly authorizing first dispatch and all safe local ORCHESTOR-core work. Costa Clean product/application work remains forbidden.
objective: Finish ORCHESTOR completely as a standalone, clean, installable local agent for arbitrary repositories/projects: obvious ON/OFF state, zero visible terminal windows, simple project onboarding, concurrent isolated task lanes, persistent Codex-thread routing, autonomous implement-test-review-repair loops, restart recovery, human-gate notifications, and strict cross-project/worktree isolation. Continue autonomously until PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES or a genuine human safety/approval gate that cannot be resolved inside this authority.
why: The user wants ORCHESTOR to feel like a reusable agent rather than scripts tied to Costa Clean. The current runtime, zero-visible-window remediation, control-plane connection, workstream binding and durable run foundation are already partially implemented. This command authorizes completing the productized system end-to-end without further routine copy/paste.
scope: Continue from the current local ORCHESTOR source at C:\Users\USUARIO\orchestor and preserve already-passing zero-visible-window work. Do not restart from scratch.

Explicitly authorize FIRST_DISPATCH for ORCHESTOR core through the existing safe runtime once command/workstream/thread/run identity is valid. Do not require another human approval merely to start safe local ORCHESTOR-core execution.

If the previous run ar_78dc2b7e-5346-4241-9b86-d5707c1e734e is still semantically valid for the superseded command transition, reconcile it safely; otherwise create exactly one new durable run for this superseding command. Never duplicate a live run or thread.
Build ORCHESTOR as a standalone agent/service layer independent of Costa Clean application code. Costa Clean is only one registered project integration.

Create a global ORCHESTOR home outside project repositories, preferably under the normal per-user application-data location, for projects, workstreams, tasks, runs, threads, locks, logs, cache, notifications and isolated worktrees.
Keep repositories clean. Project-local ORCHESTOR metadata must be optional/minimal; prefer central state. Never place runtime logs, run state, locks or caches in arbitrary product repos.
Provide an extremely simple normal-user control surface showing ORCHESTOR ON/OFF/PAUSED/NEEDS_YOU plus active projects/tasks. No terminal should be required for routine operation.
Provide a Windows user-level launch/startup experience that can be installed or launched like an agent/app without administrator privileges and without visible PowerShell/cmd/conhost popups.

Implement a minimal tray and/or local dashboard experience with clear ON, OFF/Pause, Open Dashboard, project list, active task list, NEEDS_YOU gates, completed work and errors. Keep advanced technical state behind an optional details view.

Provide project onboarding: Add Project -> choose/local repo -> detect Git repository, GitHub remote when available, canonical branch, package/test tooling and existing Codex binding -> validate -> activate.
Support arbitrary repositories, not only JavaScript projects. Tooling detection may be plugin/capability based and must fail closed when unsupported rather than guessing.
Provide project management actions: add/register, list, inspect/status, doctor, pause, resume, disable/remove binding and safe recovery after restart.

Model concurrent work as isolated task lanes/workstreams. Each task lane gets unique projectId, workstreamId/taskId, runId, persistent Codex threadId, branch/worktree, locks, results and review-loop state.
Allow multiple projects to progress concurrently and multiple tasks within one project when their scopes/worktrees are isolated.
Never run two turns concurrently on the same persistent Codex thread. Thread usage is sequential and lock-protected.
Add conflict detection for task scopes touching overlapping files/areas. Conflicting tasks within one repo must be serialized or paused rather than racing.
Enforce hard repository/worktree sandboxing before every write: resolved repo root, worktree root, branch, task/workstream identity and allowed scope must match. Cross-project writes fail closed.
Keep the proven StrategicCommand -> validate -> dispatch -> implement -> test -> review -> repair -> recertify loop, but generalize it for arbitrary projects and task lanes.
Implement bounded automatic repair loops for normal findings. Repairable tests/lint/typecheck/build/review findings must not require human copy/paste.
Handle delayed Codex/GitHub review arrival with robust bounded polling/backoff and exact-current-head review validation.
Provide durable restart/crash recovery, command idempotency, dispatch acknowledgement, UNKNOWN-outcome fail-closed behavior and duplicate suppression.

Provide human gates only for genuinely sensitive actions: application merge, production deployment/mutation, remote database mutation, secrets/credentials, DNS, billing/payments, destructive remote actions, real external communications or material scope/authority expansion.
A human gate must create exactly one durable NEEDS_YOU intervention/notification. Unrelated safe projects/tasks must continue running.
Provide user notifications when a task completes, fails unrecoverably or reaches NEEDS_YOU. Notifications must not require visible terminal windows.

Preserve zero-visible-window guarantees for all background-reachable child/grandchild execution paths, including Git, Codex app-server, executor, reviewer, publisher, updater, notification and recovery paths.
Use the existing authenticated Codex app-server/session path only. No OPENAI_API_KEY and no direct separately-billed OpenAI API.
Support at least two projects/workstreams and at least three concurrent/queued task lanes in final certification, including two tasks in the same repo and one task in another fixture repo.
Demonstrate that two non-conflicting tasks in the same repo can progress independently via separate worktrees/threads while an overlapping-scope task is safely serialized.
Demonstrate one automatic review finding -> repair -> tests -> rereview cycle without manual prompt copy/paste.
Demonstrate daemon/process restart during active work and correct resume without duplicate dispatch, duplicate thread or duplicate publication.
Demonstrate one NEEDS_YOU gate on one task while another project continues safely.
Create an installable/portable user-level distribution suitable for reuse on another Windows machine. It must include a clear first-run/onboarding path and unambiguous ON/OFF state.
Document how to attach a new project, bind/reuse a Codex thread, create a task, inspect status, pause/resume, approve a gate, recover after restart and fully stop ORCHESTOR.

Prefer a small maintainable architecture over unnecessary frameworks. Choose the lightest UI/packaging approach that meets the user experience and zero-visible-window requirements; justify the choice in docs.
Add a one-command or one-click local development/test launch path and a production-like installed/portable launch path.
Run complete unit/integration/E2E/adversarial certification. Continue repairing safe in-scope issues automatically until all completion criteria pass.
Publish factual milestone/final evidence to the ORCHESTOR tracker/control plane and leave ORCHESTOR in a usable normal mode.
Do not stop for routine implementation questions. Make reasonable technical choices within scope and document them.
Stop only for a genuine human gate or when bounded no-progress/adversarial safety guards prove autonomous continuation unsafe.
outOfScope: Costa Clean product/application feature work, including N5.3/N5.4/N5.5 or unrelated app changes.
Production deployment or production mutation for Costa Clean or any real user project during ORCHESTOR certification.
DNS, billing, payment or real external communication changes.
Privileged Windows service installation or administrator-only system changes.
Direct OpenAI API integration or OPENAI_API_KEY dependency.
Using real production repositories as destructive concurrency test fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES is backed by full end-to-end evidence, not only unit tests.
ORCHESTOR presents a simple normal-user ON/OFF/PAUSED/NEEDS_YOU state without requiring a terminal for routine operation.
No visible PowerShell/cmd/conhost/terminal popup occurs during normal background operation, dispatch, Git/control polling, Codex execution, review, repair, publication, restart or notification.
ORCHESTOR can be installed/launched as a reusable user-level agent on Windows without administrator privileges.
A new arbitrary repository can be registered through a simple onboarding flow and validated without Costa Clean-specific hard-coding.
Global runtime state lives outside product repos; project repos remain clean except optional minimal config.
At least two independent projects/workstreams can progress concurrently with strict isolation.
At least two non-conflicting tasks in one repository can progress via separate worktrees/thread bindings without contaminating each other.
Overlapping task scopes are detected and serialized rather than raced.
Exactly one active persistent Codex thread exists per task lane/workstream and is reused sequentially.
No cross-project or cross-worktree write is possible under normal, adversarial, restart or malformed-command tests.
StrategicCommands/tasks are detected and dispatched automatically without routine human prompt copy/paste.
Safe review/test findings are repaired automatically through bounded loops until clean.
Delayed review polling, current-head validation and stale-review rejection are proven.
Restart/crash recovery resumes exact ownership/state with no duplicate side effects.
Human-gated actions generate exactly one NEEDS_YOU intervention/notification while unrelated tasks continue.
Add/list/status/doctor/pause/resume/disable/remove workflows exist and are documented/tested.
A simple task creation/status experience exists for multiple concurrent task lanes.
Full ORCHESTOR tests, lint/typecheck/build/security/static-architecture checks pass.
Final multi-project/multi-task E2E certification passes with zero production/remote destructive mutation.
No direct OpenAI API usage or OPENAI_API_KEY dependency is introduced.
Costa Clean application/product source mutations for this command = 0.
Final tracker report includes install/use steps, architecture summary, certification evidence, known non-blocking limitations and PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES.
requiredApprovals: Any production deployment or production mutation.
Any Supabase or other remote database mutation.
Any secret/credential creation, rotation or disclosure.
Any DNS, billing, payment or real external communication.
Any material expansion outside ORCHESTOR-core productization and non-production certification.
stopConditions: A forbidden or approval-required real-world side effect becomes necessary.
Zero-visible-window behavior regresses and cannot be repaired safely.
Persistent-thread identity cannot be proven without creating ambiguous duplicate ownership.
Autonomous repair reaches bounded no-progress limits with unresolved correctness/security findings.
Completion would require privileged Windows changes or direct OpenAI API usage.
A real user/project repo would need destructive mutation for certification.
verificationRequirements: Record exact ORCHESTOR source root and starting state.
Prove zero Costa Clean product/application source mutation.
Prove first dispatch and subsequent autonomous loop execution through ORCHESTOR itself.
Prove zero-visible-window background operation through extended real Windows observation covering dispatch/review/repair/restart.
Run registry, scheduler, task-lane, worktree, sandbox, thread-lock and conflict-detection tests.
Run multi-project and same-project multi-task concurrency tests.
Run NEEDS_YOU intervention/notification idempotency tests with unrelated task continuation.
Run full suite and configured lint/typecheck/build/security/static-architecture checks.
Build and smoke-test the installable/portable user-level distribution.
Perform adversarial final review and require no unresolved correctness/security findings.

Publish final tracker evidence with PROJECT_COMPLETE, INSTALLABLE_AGENT, UI_STATE_MODEL, MULTI_PROJECT, MULTI_TASK, CONFLICT_SERIALIZATION, MANUAL_COPY_PASTE_REQUIRED, ZERO_VISIBLE_WINDOWS, THREAD_POLICY, REVIEW_REPAIR_LOOP, RESTART_RECOVERY, HUMAN_GATES, NOTIFICATIONS, TESTS, FINAL_CERTIFICATION, APP_SOURCE_MUTATIONS, PRODUCTION_MUTATIONS and REMAINING_BLOCKERS.
